title: Take modesty one step at a time
whyMatters: Modesty is part of Islamic character and part of worship. New Muslims usually run into some mix of cultural pressure, family reactions, feelings about their own body, and rules at work. Growing into it sincerely, a bit at a time, holds up better than a panicked overhaul.

exactActions.text: Learn the purpose before the wardrobe
subSteps: Modesty covers clothing, speech, where you let your eyes go, behavior, and how you carry yourself.
Do not shrink the whole subject down to one garment or one culture's style.
Ask a qualified teacher what applies in your situation.

exactActions.text: Make one change you can keep
subSteps: Choose looser or more covering clothes that you find comfortable.
Put together two or three outfits you can pray in.
Do not buy a whole new wardrobe because someone pushed you into it.
Some people will see the change and ask about it.
Keep your answer calm and short.
If a visible change puts you in danger at home, get local support before you go any further.

obstacles.problem: People are pressuring me to change everything
obstacles.solution: Pressure is not the same thing as guidance. Ask a qualified, kind teacher what the priorities are, then take steps you can actually keep.
Find out what is religiously required of you first, then look at your practical options. If you need an accommodation, get local advice and keep the request specific.

tinyVersion: Pick out one modest, comfortable outfit you can pray in.
unlocksNext: Taking modesty calmly makes worship easier and leaves you steadier in your own skin.

contextNotes.title: Family safety
contextNotes.body: If a visible change is likely to provoke hostility at home, talk to a local mentor you trust before you make it.
